title: Security for data in motion (encryption, IAM, and audit)
hook: Every byte in transit and at rest during migration needs encryption, least-privilege IAM, and audit trails. A fast DataSync task with a overprivileged role is a compliance incident waiting for an auditor.

blocks.text: In transit: TLS for DataSync, HTTPS for S3, TLS for Kinesis. At rest: SSE-S3 or SSE-KMS on buckets. IAM: task-specific roles scoped to prefix not bucket-wide s3:*. Audit: CloudTrail management and data events, S3 access logging, DataSync task reports. VPC endpoints keep traffic off public internet from private subnets.

blocks.text: Migration weekends create temporary broad IAM roles that never get tightened. KMS key policy missing replication role causes silent FAILED replication. Public bucket during rushed cutover is a headline. Senior architects document who can decrypt, who can audit, and enforce SecureTransport.

blocks.title: Interview framing
blocks.body: Say: TLS in transit, SSE-KMS at rest, prefix-scoped IAM, CloudTrail data events, deny insecure transport bucket policy.

snippet.label: CloudFormation — bucket encryption and public block
snippet.code:
Resources:
  MigrationBucket:
    Type: AWS::S3::Bucket
    Properties:
      BucketName: migration-landing-prod
      BucketEncryption:
        ServerSideEncryptionConfiguration:
          - ServerSideEncryptionByDefault:
              SSEAlgorithm: aws:kms
              KMSMasterKeyID: !GetAtt MigrationKey.Arn
      PublicAccessBlockConfiguration:
        BlockPublicAcls: true
        BlockPublicPolicy: true
        IgnorePublicAcls: true
        RestrictPublicBuckets: true
snippet.explanation: Default KMS encryption on every object. Public access fully blocked.

snippet.label: Bucket policy — deny non-TLS access
snippet.explanation: Denies any HTTP request — forces HTTPS for DataSync and application uploads.

snippet.label: IAM policy — DataSync role prefix scope
snippet.explanation: ListBucket on bucket ARN; object actions only on incoming/ prefix. KMS for SSE-KMS objects.

snippet.label: CLI — enable CloudTrail data events on prefix
snippet.explanation: Data events cost per event — scope to sensitive prefix not entire account.

blocks.title: Pitfalls to avoid
blocks.body: Migration role with s3:* and kms:*. Forgetting replication role in KMS key policy. CloudTrail data events on all buckets — cost explosion. Temporary public bucket 'just for testing'.

blocks.text: How to prove it in production: IAM Access Analyzer findings on migration roles. S3 Block Public Access account-level setting. Macie scan on landing bucket for PII before promoting to prod. Post-migration: delete overprivileged roles — automate with IaC only.

blocks.title: What gets you rejected in interviews
blocks.body: Saying 'S3 is private so we are secure.' Strong answer: encryption at rest and in transit, least-privilege IAM, audit data events, block public access, KMS key policies for replication.

interviewTakeaways: Encrypt in transit (TLS) and at rest (SSE-KMS); deny insecure transport in bucket policy.
IAM roles scoped to prefix; KMS key policies for each service role.
CloudTrail data events on sensitive prefixes — not entire account.
60s: SSE-KMS CMK. Prefix IAM. Deny HTTP. CloudTrail data events. Block public access. Tighten roles post-migration.
Follow-up: cross-account replication KMS key policy?
commonPitfalls: DataSync role with full bucket admin — rejection in security review.
Strong answer: PutObject/List on specific prefix only plus KMS grants.
KMS key policy missing s3 replication role — FAILED replication.
Account-wide data events — unnecessary CloudTrail cost.

jsTsCorrelations.note: Presigned PUT limited to key prefix resembles IAM resource ARN scope — time-bound and path-bound access for partner uploads.
Express redirect HTTP to HTTPS parallels S3 bucket policy aws:SecureTransport deny — enforce encryption in transit at infrastructure boundary.
